model.scope: Same complete synthetic facility with explicit finite reserve actors and paid sensible backup cooling; not as-built Zhengzhou or calibrated tower performance.

R0.scope: Research facility choices; no empirical parameter calibration.

Z1.scope: 2025 procurement scope supports module categories, not chosen capacities, locations or backup coverage.

Z2.scope: 2026 medium-voltage/HVDC and phase-change architecture statement; exact feeders and coolant properties remain unknown.

Z3.scope: 2025 lake-water/plate-HX/internal-water functional chain; not commissioning data.

Rrun.scope: Explicit low-order synthetic M1 operating point, equations and validity; not site calibration.

Rprop.scope: Frozen CoolProp 8.0.0 HEOS/R134a DEF equilibrium surrogate; actual Zhengzhou coolant unknown.

Rwater.scope: Synthetic series-valve characteristic, shutoff interlock and independent water engineering checks; no field calibration.

Renv.scope: Declared hot-water leakage, sensible floor-water storage, risk-only condensation boundary and independent access-permission engineering model; not site calibration.

Rpsychro.scope: Verify ASHRAE 2017 ch.1 eq.6 liquid-water saturation-pressure coefficients only. No moisture/latent-heat model or dispatch evidence is imported.

R09.scope: Bounded deterministic local measurement offsets, validity and supervisory autonomy; not site calibration.

Rreserve.scope: Finite autonomous UPS/generator control, starter inventory, common distribution and sensible cooler; explicit research design, not site facts.

lake_water.description: Lake water is kept separate from internal circulation.

internal_water.description: Research internal water loop, not lake water or phase coolant.

thermal_transfer.description: Energy transfer across an interface, not a mass connection.

floor_water.description: Distinct floor-water pool mixing external ambient nuisance water and explicitly transferred hot internal water; same assumed constant cp, no cooling return path.

Internal-water pump is hydraulically lumped into the loop, electrically explicit, and its total electrical heat is allocated once between fluid and room.
Heat graph edges across plate HX are accounting aliases of the enthalpy transfer; do not add them a second time.
Generator has finite fuel and an ideal start delay; backup tower is standby/uncommanded in M1, pending ticket 10.
Nuisance floor water is a separate ambient external source; humidity is a fixed boundary and no coolant leak is modeled in M1.
worker_control is dual-qualified for control/cooling, shares the one portable flow meter, and all jobs are finite predeclared engineering requests.
Water-v3 adds two aggregate series valves, each with independent Kopen/a^2, and preserves v2 full-open total resistance and thermal initialization.

Valve openings are imposed actual plant states in engineering inputs. A zero opening immediately stops its own pump through a declared local hardwired interlock; static trapped pressures, deadhead heating, leakage and actuator dynamics are outside this model.
Valve/pipe pressure drops are differential dynamic losses, not gauge pressures. Their hydraulic dissipation is already inside each pump total electrical heat allocation and is not added again.
Positive openings whose derived resistance cannot be represented finitely are outside the numerical domain and fail explicitly.
Environment-v4 starts at the same healthy water-v3 working point; actual hot-water leakage defaults to zero and gate permission to one.

Remaining hot-water mass changes its thermal capacity. Hydraulic behavior is valid only at or above the declared minimum hot inventory; below it the run fails without inventing suction geometry or clipping inventory.
Hot leakage exports cp*T using the same zero-K sensible reference as the liquid inventory and floor pool; pressure work and kinetic/elevation terms are outside this bounded incompressible model.

The separate external nuisance-water source and initial floor pool are at the declared ambient temperature. The floor pool mixes adiabatically and drains at its evolving actual temperature; no evaporation, latent heat or floor-to-room transfer is modeled.
Air sensible storage and liquid heat remain separately accounted. RH is an imposed diagnostic boundary with no moisture-mass inventory or condensate production.

Cold-buffer bulk temperature is an explicit proxy for an exposed cold surface, not a wall/insulation model. The risk criterion uses liquid-water saturation only at 273.16 to 333.15 K, without extrapolation.

IT access requires binary gate permission, open environmental conditions and the independent access graph with all qualifications/tools. A gate closes work permission but does not erase elapsed labor or move personnel/tools.

The explicit room work-temperature threshold closes on rising crossing and opens on falling crossing. Equality uses the direction of the continuous sensible-temperature trajectory; a stationary initial equality is closed. No step-sized extra work is granted.
UPS internal control and generator internal control/cranking have distinct finite paid supply; they do not depend on an unsupplied main PLC.
Generator starter energy is a separate ideal DC store inside the generator asset; no recharge is modeled. Its output dissipates outside once.
The shared distribution enclosure gates normal and protected rails under one explicit common cause, while UPS coverage remains only the original three auxiliary loads.
The effective standby sensible exchanger shares one actual internal circulation capacity with the mutually exclusive primary path, adds no water mass, and has no evaporation model.
Fan and generator control/cranking heat exits outside; UPS internal control heat enters the room. Site tower/storage/coverage data remain unresolved.
